title: The referee watches again
text: No invention has divided football like the video assistant referee, whose screen {{1}} quietly above every major match. The promise was {{2}}: clear up the notorious errors that decide titles and careers. The practice has been messier. Decisions take longer, and the game has discovered that most offside calls are not {{3}} at all — they are a boot's width of pixel, agonised over by analysts while the stadium holds its {{4}}. Supporters who wanted fairness got fairness, and {{5}} that they preferred atmosphere. The {{6}} has settled into a compromise: interventions only for clear errors, with lines drawn thicker and the benefit of the doubt returned to attackers. What the experiment has {{7}} is how much of football's joy rests on imperfection — on human pace, human eyesight and the roar that {{8}} when the assistant referee raises the flag and is, or is not, overruled.

gaps.explanation: 'whose screen hovers quietly above' — stays suspended; hoist = lift with ropes, hibernate = spend the winter asleep.
'the promise was simple' — plain and clear; simplistic is pejorative, implying the promise ignored complications.
'most offside calls are not obvious at all' — not clear to the eye; oblivious = unaware.
'the stadium holds its breath' — the fixed idiom takes the noun 'breath'; breathe is the verb.
'supporters who wanted fairness got fairness, and protested that they preferred atmosphere' — objected; prosper and prolong do not take that-clauses, and promote does not fit the complaint.
'the standoff has settled into a compromise' — the situation where neither side would yield; standpoint = a point of view.
'what the experiment has exposed' — revealed, often uncomfortably; exhibit = put on display.
'the roar that erupts when the flag goes up' — bursts out like a volcano; elope = run away to marry.
